CBC Uncivil Dialogue: Commenting and stories about Indigenous Peoples

As I said over at /v/CanadianPolitics regarding this story.......

There are a great many myths and misconceptions out there regarding the Crowns relationship with, and responsibilities toward, Aboriginal peoples in Canada. Unfortunately these myths and misconceptions have been played upon by governments, political parties, racists, and those with agendas that run counter to those legally binding and constitutionally protected treaties and modern day comprehensive land claims agreements.

I've had the discussion many times with different people, and the discussion is almost always the same. Detractors tend to feel that that the government should be bound by legal contracts (which is exactly what treaties and modern day comprehensive land claims agreements are) except when it comes to treaties and modern day comprehensive land claims agreements.

These contracts, many feel, are ridiculous, outdated, and overly generous and should be changed - but unlike other legally binding contracts the government should be able to simply impose new terms instead of negotiate them, and/or ignore the terms of these legally binding contracts, and/or spend hundreds of millions of dollars in the courts fighting implementation of these contracts.

That's not how either contract or constitutional law works.

When it comes down to it many of the comments seen in news articles regarding Aboriginal people are rooted in one of two things

  1. racism and/or bigotry

  2. ignorance regarding treaties and modern day comprehensive land claims agreements and the Crowns responsibilities and obligations under them.

The answer is to inform and educate people - unfortunately you can do neither with those who consider political rhetoric and bigoted Facebook memes as authoritative.
